channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: CITIZENS — PHOTO IS:RAEL Open Call 2026
item.description: Open call for the 13th International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv (October 2026), themed around citizenship and photography as active civic practice — grassroots perspectives, democratic engagement, and belonging beyond legal status. Open to artists worldwide at all career stages, with existing or new projects. Photography, film, video, performance documentation, animation, and hybrid/digital forms are accepted; up to 12 images per submission. Selected artists are shown in the festival's Main Exhibition, included in the 2026 catalog, and featured on the festival website. — Deadline: July 28, 2026. Fee: $22. Prize: Exhibition in festival Main Exhibition + 2026 catalog.

item.title: Penland Winter Residency 2027
item.description: A self-directed project residency during Penland's quiet winter season, offering artists two- or four-week sessions of studio time and equipment access with no classes, assignments or critiques. Residents work independently in one of Penland's teaching studios — photography is among the available studios, alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, papermaking, printmaking, textiles and wood — with studio assistants on hand for orientation and equipment help. Sessions run January 3–15 and January 17–29, 2027; the residency fee is $500 for two weeks (more for flameworking and hot shop) plus housing, and limited fellowships cover the residency fee and partial housing, with preference given to first-time applicants and artists from underrepresented backgrounds. Open to artists at any career stage who are comfortable working independently. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $30 application. Prize: 2–4 week residency.

item.title: 12th International Phone-ography Competition · FotoFoto Gallery
item.description: FotoFoto Gallery, a cooperative photography gallery in Huntington, New York, holds its 12th annual international competition exclusively for images shot on phone cameras — 'Image capture must have been made with the camera on your phone. Any phone!' Around 30 photographs are selected by juror Karen Klinedinst for the gallery exhibition, August 27 – September 19, 2026, with cash awards of $300, $200 and $100. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide (gallery members excluded); 5–15 images. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $40 (5 images), $5 each additional. Prize: $600 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 63rd Stockton Art League Juried Exhibition
item.description: Established in 1951, the Stockton Art League presents its 63rd national juried exhibition at the Haggin Museum in Stockton, California, September 3 – October 25, 2026. Accepted media explicitly include photography, analog and digital, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, mixed media and assemblage. Juried by Francesca Wilmott, Curator at the Crocker Art Museum, with the $1,000 Ruby Zahn White Best of Show, $500 second place, $250 third place and merit awards. Open to US-based artists; work completed within the last two years. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $35 first entry, $5 each additional (up to 5). Prize: $1,750+ in cash awards.

item.title: 47th Annual National Juried Art Show · Arts Council of Wayne County
item.description: The Arts Council of Wayne County runs its 47th annual national juried show in downtown Goldsboro, North Carolina, October 2–30, 2026. Accepted media explicitly include photography alongside drawings, paintings, printmaking, graphics, sculpture, ceramics, textiles and mixed media. Juried by Sally Jacobs, Assistant Director of the Artist Innovation Mentorship Program at the North Carolina Museum of Art, with $1,950 in awards: $1,000 Best in Show, $500 second, $250 third, plus $100 each for Best in Wayne County and People's Choice. Open to US artists 18+; original work created within the last two years, for sale. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 4 images). Prize: $1,950 in cash awards.

item.title: Ghosts & Things Regional Exhibition · Texarkana Regional Arts & Humanities Council
item.description: TRAHC's annual regional juried exhibition takes a supernatural 'Ghosts & Things' theme for 2026, showing September 12 – November 21 at the Regional Arts Center in downtown Texarkana. Accepted media explicitly include photography and video alongside printmaking, sculpture, aquamedia, oils, acrylic, fiber arts, collage, intermedia and drawing. A low $15 flat fee covers up to three entries, with $500, $300, $150 and $50 awards. Open to artists 18+ residing in Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma or Texas; original work completed 2021–2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: SCA Open 2026
item.description: The Sausalito Center for the Arts' statewide open juried exhibition runs October 30 – December 6, 2026 at 750 Bridgeway, judged by a notably strong jury: Nancy Lim (Associate Curator of Painting and Sculpture, SFMOMA), Danielle Fox (Director, SLATE Contemporary) and painter Chester Arnold. Work in all mediums except video and AI-generated artwork is welcome — the prospectus explicitly lists photography. Open to California residents 18+; new submissions only, hand delivery of accepted work required. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $35 first work, $10 each additional (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Point of Hue · Ashton Gallery @ Art on 30th
item.description: A color-themed national juried exhibition at Ashton Gallery inside San Diego's Art on 30th complex, November 7 – December 4, 2026, juried by Southern California arts and museum leader Daniel Foster. Accepted media explicitly include photography alongside acrylic, oils, watercolor, drawing, assemblage, collage, encaustic, mixed media, fiber art and pedestal-scale 3D work; no digital art, reproductions or AI art. $1,000 in cash awards (Best in Show, First Place, Juror's Choice, Honorable Mentions) and a printed exhibition catalog. Open to US artists; works must be for sale, 10–72 inches. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $40 first entry, $5 per additional (up to 6). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: 36th Annual All Florida Juried Art Show · MartinArts
item.description: MartinArts' statewide juried survey, in its 36th year, exhibits January 8 – March 10, 2027 at the Court House Cultural Center in Stuart, Florida. All media are accepted, with photography expressly permitted — it is the only medium in which giclées or editions may be entered. Juried by independent curator Lisa Rockford (Rockford Projects), with $500, $200 and $100 prizes plus up to four $50 honorable mentions. Open to professional artists across Florida. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 images), $35 members. Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: SMALL WORKS 2026 · Jag Gallery
item.description: Jag Gallery's annual small-works juried holiday exhibition runs December 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027 at 1075 Duval Street in Key West. Work must be current, original and no larger than 10 inches in any direction including the frame; accepted media explicitly include photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture and textile (no jewelry or AI). Juror's Choice, People's Choice and four Honorable Mention award winners are invited to the 2027 Award Winners group show. Open to artists 18+, international submissions accepted. — Deadline: October 24, 2026. Fee: $18 per piece (up to 6). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 60th National Mother Lode Art Exhibition · Placerville Arts Association
item.description: The Placerville Arts Association's National Mother Lode Art Exhibition reaches its 60th edition — a six-decade Northern California institution — showing November 5–21, 2026 at the Mills Station Arts and Culture Center (The MACC) in Rancho Cordova. All media except installations are considered, with photography explicitly listed; photography and digital art are the only media permitted as editions. Juried and judged by mixed-media artist Debra Kreck-Harnish, with over $4,250 in awards including a $700 Best of Show. Open to US-based artists; original work created 2023 or later. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $25 first work, $15 each additional (up to 10). Prize: $4,250+ in cash awards.

item.title: Royal Society Publishing Photography Competition 2026
item.description: The Royal Society's publishing arm runs this annual competition celebrating photography by working scientists — treating the research image as visual culture in its own right, across Astronomy, Behaviour, Earth Science and Climatology, Ecology and Environmental Science, and Microimaging. The overall winner receives £1,000; category winners receive £500 plus Royal Photographic Society certificates and one-year memberships. Open to anyone studying or working in science at graduate level or above; up to 20 entries per person. Free to enter. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000.

item.title: The Nature Photography Contest 2026 · The Nature Photography Contest
item.description: International online nature photography competition across ten categories — Natural Landscapes, Wildlife, Macro, Underwater, Birds, Plant Life, Night World, Environmental Impact, Sharing the Planet and Funny Nature — with conservation built into the entry model: every participant funds a tree through One Tree Planted, and winners choose where planting happens. Photography of the Year wins €1,000, with €100 for each category winner; finalists must supply original RAW/DNG files for verification, and digital art is not accepted. Open worldwide to photographers 18+. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: €10 per photograph. Prize: €2,000 in cash prizes.

item.title: reFocus Awards - World Photo Annual 2026
item.description: reFocus's flagship annual competition across 22 categories — from abstract, architecture and fine art to photojournalism, street, wildlife and film/analog — crowning an International Photographer of the Year and Discovery of the Year alongside gold, silver and bronze category winners. Over $5,000 in cash prizes, with winners receiving a published interview, online exhibition and international media exposure. Judged by photo editors and creative directors from The New York Times, Robb Report, Financial Times HTSI, Condé Nast Traveller UK and Rizzoli. Single images or series of 2–5; tiered fees from $17 with early-bird pricing through August 26, rising toward the October 21 final deadline; winners announced December 9, 2026. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $17–$50. Prize: $5,000+ in cash prizes.

item.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #139 — Food 2026
item.description: Photography of and about food, for the October/November 2026 issue of F-Stop Magazine, the online photography magazine publishing themed issues since 2004. Submit up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. One submission per person per issue; selected work appears on the magazine site as part of its permanent archive. Publication expected October 1, 2026. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 73 — Editorial Submissions
item.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 73 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. First-round deadline July 18; second-round August 18 if space remains. Issue release August 21, 2026. Editorials must be unpublished, with a minimum of 5 outfit changes (or 5 hair/make-up looks for beauty) and at least 3 retouched photos per look. Send via PDF, Dropbox, or WeTransfer. — Deadline: August 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 101 Art Book: Pattern Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: Arts to Hearts Project selects 101 artists for a hardcover art book exploring Pattern as a visual and conceptual theme — repetition, rhythm, structure and surface — distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble and the ATH shop. All visual art forms are welcome, photography explicitly included. The top-selected artist receives a USD 500 cash award alongside publication; all selected artists are published in the book. Thirteenth edition in the 101 Art Book series; open to artists 18+ worldwide at all career stages. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500.

item.title: Arts to Hearts Magazine Issue 14 — The Summer We Remember
item.description: Themed issue of Arts to Hearts Magazine inviting work on 'The Summer We Remember' — memories, moments and metaphors of summer. Open to artists 18+ worldwide across painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, printmaking, digital art, collage, textile, mixed media, installation and illustration. The winner receives a USD 500 cash prize, a 4-page spread and a glass trophy; two runners-up get 4-page spreads and trophies, and all selected artists receive a 2-page spread in the internationally distributed magazine. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants — Cycle 37 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. Open to visual artists — photography explicitly included, traditional and experimental — plus film/video, digital/electronic arts and choreography. Applicants must be 21+, reside in the United States, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, show sustained public-facing artistic activity over the past five years, and meet the income cap ($80,000 individual / $160,000 joint, averaged over the last two tax returns). Cycle 37 covers emergencies occurring December 1, 2025 onward. — Deadline: July 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.

item.title: 13th Eurostars Madrid Tower Photography Award — Madrid's Facades
item.description: The 13th edition of the free annual photography award run by the five-star Eurostars Madrid Tower hotel, themed 'Madrid's facades' — textures, balconies, geometry and unexpected corners of the city's buildings, from classical restraint to contemporary towers. First prize €5,000 plus a trophy, with a €3,000 Hotusa Group award and eight runner-up hotel stays; winning images are exhibited and used in the hotel's interior design. Open to photographers 18+ of any nationality; up to 3 unpublished photographs, max 6 MB per file, submitted via the online form. — Deadline: January 25, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 + €3,000 runner-up.

item.title: Flowing & Flying: A National Exhibit of Waterbirds and Waterscapes · d'Art Center
item.description: A national juried exhibition at d'Art Center, the nonprofit art center in Norfolk, Virginia's NEON District, dedicated to waterscapes — ocean, lakes, ponds, rivers, wetlands and swamps — and the birds that inhabit them. All mediums and styles are welcome, 2D or 3D, making it a natural fit for nature and wildlife photographers. Open to US artists 18+ with original work made in the last 8 years; up to 10 works. Juried by Val Parnell, with $950 in cash awards; exhibition August 22 – September 19, 2026. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $950 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: TOKAS-Emerging 2027
item.description: Annual emerging-artist program at Tokyo Arts and Space, the contemporary art arm of the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo. Four artists aged 35 or younger and based in Japan are each selected for a solo exhibition on their own floor of TOKAS Hongo in April–May 2027, with ¥150,000 in production support plus installation assistance, transport subsidies, PR support, and an exhibition catalog. Eligible fields include painting, printmaking, photography, three-dimensional work, video, and installation; group applications are accepted if all members qualify. The application package is available in Japanese only; second-round interviews take place September 18, 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + ¥150,000 production support.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — October 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the October issue runs August 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Virtual Artist Residency — Fall 2026
item.description: 10-week virtual residency (September 4 – November 6, 2026) for artists who work with or are inspired by found/family photographs. Weekly Zoom calls, bio/statement workshops, artist talks, group feedback, and accountability groups in a cohort of 6–9 artists. Open worldwide to artists at any career stage and in any medium, as long as found or family photography informs the work; participants commit to attending at least 80% of weekly calls. Partial scholarships available. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $650. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Lanesboro Juried Sales Gallery 2027
item.description: Lanesboro Arts' Juried Sales Gallery in Lanesboro, Minnesota represents more than 80 regional artists on consignment, with artists receiving 60% of the retail price. Applications for 2027 representation are open to artists residing in Minnesota, Iowa, and Wisconsin; all visual arts media are eligible, including photography, and work must be for sale. Jurying is by practicing artists and arts professionals with regional connections. Online applications preferred; hard-copy and video applications accepted. Notification by February 26, 2027. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Gallery representation + exhibition.

item.title: New Visionary Magazine Issue 18 · Visionary Art Collective
item.description: Print-magazine open call curated by Michelle Brandt, founder and director of Brandt Gallery and Pecha Projects. Selected artists receive a two-page spread in New Visionary Magazine featuring a Q&A interview and multiple images of their work. Open internationally to artists at all career stages working in all 2D and 3D mediums, including photography. Tiered fees: $30 for 3–4 images, $35 for 5–6, $40 for 7–8. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $30–40. Prize: Publication (2-page spread + interview).

item.title: Source Writing Prize 2026
item.description: Annual writing prize from Source, the Belfast-based quarterly of contemporary photography, open to writers who have not previously written for the magazine. Submit one original, unpublished piece of up to 700 words about photography from any angle — a book or exhibition review, an introduction to a photographer's work, or a historical, aesthetic, cultural, or philosophical take on the medium. The winner receives £500/€570 plus publication in Source or a future paid commission; shortlisted entries are also considered for publication and commissions. Chosen by editor Richard West and Source staff. Deadline 5:30pm GMT. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £500 + publication.

item.title: The Tom Stoddart Award in Collaboration with GOST Books · Ian Parry Foundation
item.description: Photobook award from the Ian Parry Foundation honoring photojournalist Tom Stoddart, run in collaboration with independent publisher GOST Books. Open worldwide to established photographers (18+) working in long-form documentary photography with an in-depth project nearing completion and suitable for a book. The recipient's project is published by GOST as a clothbound hardback with worldwide distribution, supported by a £5,000 grant paid in two installments toward expenses and travel to Verona to oversee printing, plus media coverage by The Guardian. Submit a biography, project description, and up to 40 representative images, with an optional PDF of book design. No AI-generated or digitally manipulated imagery. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: £50. Prize: Photobook publication + £5,000.

item.title: Art Moves 2026 — International Billboard Art Competition
item.description: International billboard art competition of the Art Moves Festival in Toruń, Poland, on the theme 'Fear or courage? How can we stop fearing tomorrow and start creating it together?' (theme use encouraged but not mandatory). A jury of public-art artists and curators selects the 8 most interesting works, which are printed and displayed on billboards in Toruń's city space during the festival in September 2026; the best work receives the PLN 6,500 main award (about €1,533/$1,805). Open worldwide to individuals and groups, any technique — submit up to 3 works as 30×14.6cm 72dpi JPG previews by email. AI-generated projects are prohibited. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: PLN 6,500 (~€1,533) + billboard exhibition.

item.title: Revela'T Portfolio Review 2026
item.description: Portfolio review open call for Revela'T, the contemporary analog photography festival in Vilassar de Dalt near Barcelona (October 1–18, 2026, main weekend October 16–18). Eighteen photographers are selected for 20-minute one-to-one sessions with each of 11 reviewers — three hours of feedback — plus a full festival pass; one participant additionally wins production and exhibition of their project at Revela'T 2027. Open to photographers of any nationality or residence working in chemical or digital photography; selection favors projection, originality, and a compelling concept. Free to apply — only selected participants pay €15 (Revela'T Friends) or €25. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: Free (selected pay €15–25). Prize: Portfolio reviews + exhibition at Revela'T 2027.

item.title: AFC Nature Photography Contest 2026
item.description: Free nature photography contest from Arroyos & Foothills Conservancy, a Pasadena-based land trust protecting Southern California wildlife habitat. Seven categories — Birds, Mammals, Other Wildlife, Plants, Landscapes, People in Nature, and Abstract/Conceptual — plus a public-vote Viewer's Choice Award announced at a September event. Winning images are professionally printed at AFC's expense and displayed at a public awards event (2025 winners were shown at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County). Open to anyone 15 or older; images must have been taken in Southern California within the last 5 years. Up to 2 photos per category; manipulated images only in Abstract/Conceptual; no AI-generated images. Deadline 11:50pm PST. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + professional prints.

item.title: IVI 4th International Photo Contest
item.description: Global photo contest from the International Vaccine Institute, the Seoul-based international organization devoted to vaccines for global health. Theme: 'A healthier world made possible by vaccination, available to everyone, everywhere.' Grand prize US$2,000, gold $1,000, two silver prizes of $500, six bronze prizes of $200, plus honorable mentions. Open worldwide to anyone 18 or older (IVI employees excluded); up to 5 photographs, each submitted separately via Submittable. Deadline 23:59 Korea Standard Time. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Eurostars Valladolid Photography Award — Valladolid Unveiled
item.description: Photography award from Eurostars Hotel Company on the theme 'Valladolid unveiled' — images that capture and represent the city of Valladolid, Spain, both for those who live there and those seeing it for the first time. First prize €1,500 plus a trophy; runners-up receive trophies and complimentary stays at Eurostars Hotel Company properties. Open to amateur and professional photographers 18+; up to 3 photographs, max 6 MB per file, submitted via the online form. — Deadline: September 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500.

item.title: PERSPA 2026 — Prix de la Perspective Architecturale
item.description: International architectural photography prize run by PERSPA, a French association based in Bourges. Categories span Fine Art, Aerial, Black & White, Cityscape, Minimalism, Night & Low Light, Geometry, Stairs, Historic & Heritage, Human & Architecture, and more; entries are single images. Grand prize €1,000; winning and selected works are shown in a physical exhibition in France and considered for the PERSPA annual publication. Open worldwide to professional, emerging, and independent photographers who own the rights to their work; one complimentary single-image entry for photographs taken in France. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €25 per entry. Prize: €1,000 + exhibition + publication.

item.title: Tiny But Mighty: d'Art's Annual National Exhibit of Small Artworks
item.description: Annual national juried exhibition of small artworks at d'Art Center, the nonprofit art center in Norfolk, Virginia's NEON District (est. 1986). All mediums and all styles are welcome, 2D or 3D, as long as work measures no more than 8 inches in its longest dimension (12 inches for framed hanging pieces). Open to US artists 18+; 3 to 10 works. Exhibition in The Vault gallery August 22 – September 19, 2026. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 CWA National Open Juried Exhibition
item.description: National open juried exhibition from Connecticut Women Artists, one of the country's oldest women's art organizations, founded in 1929. Open to US women artists 18+ with original work created in the past 3 years and not previously shown in a CWA exhibition; accepted media include photography, painting, mixed media, drawing, collage, printmaking, fiber and textile art, sculptural ceramics, and sculpture (no digital or AI-generated art, no photo reproductions). $2,100 in awards. Juror: Jeanne Ciravolo, director of the Alexey von Schlippe Gallery. Exhibition at Akus Gallery, Eastern Connecticut State University, Willimantic, August 26 – October 16, 2026. Up to 3 works; members $35 first entry/$12 each additional, non-members $45/$15. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: $45 first entry ($35 members). Prize: $2,100 in awards.

item.title: Sixth LaGrange Southeast Regional
item.description: Juried regional at the LaGrange Art Museum in Georgia, continuing the lineage of the LaGrange National begun in 1964. Open to artists 18+ residing in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia, with original work from the last two years in drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, photography, ceramics, or mixed media. Purchase Awards add works to permanent collections, alongside juror-selected Merit Awards; no commission on sales. Exhibition September 19, 2026 – January 9, 2027. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $45 (up to 4 works). Prize: Museum exhibition + Purchase Awards.

item.title: Unscripted · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Open-themed juried exhibition at Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit community art center in Frederick, Maryland, welcoming artwork that is free from prescribed narratives. Accepted media include painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, sculpture, fiber art, ceramics, mixed media, and digital art. Open to visual artists 18+ residing in the continental US; 1–3 images at 300 dpi for jury review. Exhibition runs August 1–30, 2026 at the Artspiration Frederick Gallery. Deadline 11:59pm EST. — Deadline: July 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Summer Open Juried Exhibition · West Portal Gallery
item.description: Summer open juried show at West Portal Gallery, a community art space in San Francisco's West Portal neighborhood. Open to artists of the greater Bay Area — San Francisco, Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, and Sonoma counties, plus Sacramento, Yolo, San Joaquin, Monterey, San Benito, and Santa Cruz. All media and styles welcome, including photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, printmaking, fiber, and digital art; 3–10 images. Exhibition August 28 – October 1, 2026, with an opening reception September 11. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3), $10 each additional. Prize: $500 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Great Northern Art Explosion · AuSable Artisan Village
item.description: Annual juried art competition at AuSable Artisan Village, a nonprofit arts center in Grayling, Michigan, with $8,000 in awards — $2,500 grand prize, $1,000 second, and $500 third in both juror and People's Choice categories. Open to artists 18+ with original work completed in the last two years and not previously shown at the Explosion; media include photography, oils, acrylic, watercolor, mixed media, ceramics, wood, metal, jewelry, sculpture, and fabric. One entry of 1–3 images per artist. Exhibition August 21 – September 6, 2026, with the awards ceremony on closing day. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $40 (1–3 images). Prize: $8,000 in awards.

item.title: 2026 Members Exhibition — Hunterdon Art Museum
item.description: Annual members exhibition at the Hunterdon Art Museum in Clinton, New Jersey. Juror Bryant Small, associate curator at the Morris Museum, selects one artist for a solo exhibition in the museum's River Gallery during the 2027–28 season, and a $100 museum prize goes to another artist. Open to current museum members — non-members may join when applying — with work from the last five years not previously shown at the museum; media include photography, sculpture, fiber, glass, printmaking, oils, acrylics, watercolors, pastel, pencil, and collage. Up to 5 images ($40 covers the first three). — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $40 (3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Solo exhibition + $100.

item.title: Call of the Wild — Virtual Exhibition 2026 · San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center
item.description: Virtual juried exhibition from the nonprofit San Fernando Valley Arts & Cultural Center exploring artists' relationships with flora and fauna in nature. Best of Show wins $800 cash plus a solo exhibition valued over $1,700; first place $400, second place $300, and up to four honorable mentions. Open to all artists and photographers worldwide; no AI-generated work. Juror: Dale Youngman, Los Angeles-based curator. Online exhibition September 1 – October 31, 2026 on sfvacc.org. Deadline 11:59pm PST. — Deadline: August 13, 2026. Fee: $40 first entry, $5 each additional. Prize: $800 + solo exhibition.

item.title: 18th Annual Juried Show — Riverviews Artspace
item.description: National juried show at Riverviews Artspace's Craddock-Terry Gallery in Lynchburg, Virginia. This edition asks artists to create contemporary reinterpretations of artworks made in 1935 or earlier — each entry needs a clear source, a contemporary perspective, and an artist statement identifying the original work and its creator. All media considered, including photography, painting, sculpture, collage, and digital work. Grand prize $750 cash plus a portfolio review; $100 Awards of Distinction; People's Choice award. Juror: Amy Calandra Davis, founder and curator of Findings Art Gallery. Deadline 11:59pm EST. — Deadline: September 12, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 works). Prize: $750 + portfolio review.

item.title: The Fridge Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: A free online exhibition honoring Blue Sky Gallery's 1990 exhibition 'The Refrigerator Show,' inviting photographers to submit images of refrigerator interiors — organized or chaotic, from tidy shelves to whatever is really chilling in the back. Part of the gallery's 50th Anniversary online exhibition series. Accepted work is shown online only and is not for sale; the exhibition opens August 6, 2026. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: BBA One Shot Award - Autumn 2026
item.description: Single-image photography prize. 20 selected images are professionally printed and exhibited at BBA Gallery in Berlin, with 50 additional images shown on a large digital display. First prize: €300 cash plus the exhibition, an Artsy profile, and social media and newsletter promotion. BBA covers all production and shipping costs for selected work. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: €19. Prize: €300.

item.title: Elemental: Earth, Air, Fire, Water · TCG Gallery
item.description: An international juried online exhibition built on the four elements — earth, air, fire and water — not merely as scenery but as pressure, weather, heat, erosion, breath, flood, smoke, stone, ash and atmosphere. Work may engage the elements directly or symbolically, exploring beauty, danger, memory, destruction, renewal and transformation. All two-dimensional images with an analog or digital photographic base are welcome, with no restrictions on size or year of production. The show runs online October 1 – November 1, 2026. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Out of Time / Out of Place · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Photographers are invited to explore imagery that disrupts chronological and geographic sense — work addressing dislocation, anachronism, nostalgia, surreal encounters, unexpected juxtapositions, or moments that resist easy placement in time and space. Documentary, conceptual, landscape, portraiture and experimental approaches are all encouraged, in color or black and white. Selected work is shown at the A Photographer's Place gallery in Raleigh (August 7–31, 2026), with a reception on August 7. — Deadline: July 23, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rebecca Morse Selects 2026 · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: An open-themed juried exhibition selected by Rebecca Morse, Curator in the Wallis Annenberg Photography Department at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), who has organized major exhibitions of work by Ed Ruscha, Barbara Kruger and Thomas Joshua Cooper. Selected work is shown at the APG Gallery in Atlanta (August 25 – September 25, 2026), with a reception on August 27. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: Members from $40 (2 works); students from $30; need-based scholarships available. Prize: $3,000 Purchase Award.

item.title: MONOCHROME · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: NYC4PA's international juried call MONOCHROME celebrates the special nature of the monochrome print — black and white, sepia, or shades of a single color — where emotion, texture and beauty are expressed in gradations from light to dark. All photographic processes and approaches are welcome. Selected images appear in an online gallery and catalog, and winning work is shown in the NYC4PA exhibition. Judging is blind. Submissions open July 5, 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $40 (first 3 images); $10 each additional. Prize: $1,100 Grand Prize.

item.title: Future Figurations Residency · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: A five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (January 25 – February 26, 2027) exploring speculative futures, science fiction, myth-making and world-building, using futurity as an anti-oppressive, restorative and decolonizing force. Artists receive individual studio space, faculty mentorship and studio visits, weekly talks and workshops, open studios, and access to specialized production facilities and the Paul D. Fleck Library and Archives. Eligible mediums explicitly include photography and digital media. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship (100% tuition plus 25% of meals and accommodation). — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: CAD $65 application fee; tuition covered by scholarship (accommodation & meals approx. CAD $4,385). Prize: Residency.
